title: JC H2 biology — ecology: energy flow and the carbon cycle

scenes.caption: Food chains: arrows follow energy flow
scenes.narration: A food chain is a sequence of trophic levels. Follow the red energy dot: it enters the grass, then moves with each feeding step — grass to rabbit to fox — because arrows point the way energy flows: food to feeder.

shape.explain: The producer: grass captures the sunlight that feeds the whole chain.
Food-chain arrow: grass -> rabbit. Energy follows the arrow.
The primary consumer: it eats the grass.
Food-chain arrow: rabbit -> fox. Energy follows the arrow.
The secondary consumer: it eats the rabbit.
One packet of energy starting its trip up the food chain.
Trophic level 1: the producers.
Trophic level 2: primary consumers eat producers.
Trophic level 3: secondary consumers eat herbivores.

steps.text: Energy travels with the arrows: food to feeder

scenes.caption: Food webs: one dot splits into two
scenes.narration: Real communities are webs, not chains. One energy dot enters the grass and splits: half travels grass to rabbit to fox, the other grass to mouse to owl. Remove one species and the ripples reach them all.

shape.explain: Grass: in this web it feeds both the rabbit and the mouse.
The rabbit: one of the fox's prey in this web.
The mouse: eaten by both fox and owl.
The fox: hunts rabbits and mice.
The owl: hunts mice from above.
Web arrow: grass -> rabbit.
Web arrow: grass -> mouse.
Web arrow: rabbit -> fox.
Web arrow: mouse -> fox.
Web arrow: mouse -> owl.
One energy packet at the producer level, about to split into two.
The same energy packet, duplicated for the web's second branch.

steps.text: Two pathways: energy splits across the web

scenes.caption: Pyramid of energy: only 10% moves up
scenes.narration: Draw energy per level and you get a pyramid. The dot shrinks as it climbs — only about a tenth of the energy becomes the next level. That is why food chains stay short.

shape.explain: The producers' energy bar: the widest bar of the pyramid.
The primary consumers' energy bar: narrower than the producers'.
Pyramid label: producers.
The secondary consumers' energy bar: narrower still.
Pyramid label: primary consumers.
The tertiary consumers' energy bar: the narrowest of all.
Pyramid label: secondary consumers.
An energy packet at the base: only about 10% climbs each level.
Pyramid label: tertiary consumers.
About 10% of the energy moves up one trophic level.

steps.text: Each level keeps only a tenth of the energy

scenes.caption: The carbon cycle: one dot, round and round
scenes.narration: Carbon loops between air and life. The blue dot drops into plants with photosynthesis, rises back with respiration and combustion, and decomposers recycle the dead — fossil fuels burn ancient carbon all at once.

shape.explain: Atmospheric CO2: the reservoir that plants draw carbon from.
Carbon arrow: CO2 moves from the air into plants.
Green plants: they fix carbon by photosynthesis.
Tells you this arrow's direction: photosynthesis draws CO2 in.
One carbon dioxide molecule on its way round the cycle.
Carbon arrow: CO2 returns to the air.
Respiration and combustion: both release CO2 back to the air.
Tells you this arrow returns CO2 to the air.
Carbon arrow: dead matter carries carbon toward decomposers.
Decomposers release carbon back into the cycle.

shape.text: fossil fuels: ancient carbon burned all at once
shape.explain: A note: burning fossil fuel dumps ancient carbon into today's air.

steps.text: Carbon loops: photosynthesis in, respiration out

scenes.caption: Conservation: when habitat shrinks, species vanish
scenes.narration: The fastest way to lose species is to lose their habitat. Watch each patch shrink under pressure — and its species label vanishes with it. Protected corridors fight back by reconnecting the fragments.

shape.explain: The first forest fragment: intact, for now.
The second fragment: isolated species start to shrink here.
The third fragment: small patches hold fewer species.
Hornbills: need large territories, vanish first.
Pangolins: trapped in shrinking fragments.
Tigers: need huge ranges; fragments cannot hold them.
The squeeze: this fragment shrinks first.
The squeeze: the second fragment follows.
The squeeze: the last fragment follows.
The protected corridor: links all three fragments.
The fix: connect fragments so genes and individuals flow.

steps.text: Habitat shrinks; species vanish with it

scenes.caption: A common mistake: energy is not recycled
scenes.narration: A common mistake: energy is recycled through the ecosystem. The "cycle of life" language makes energy sound like it loops round forever. Energy flows one way — sunlight in, heat out: the red dot enters as sunlight and leaves as heat, never returning. What is recycled is matter — carbon, nitrogen and water: the blue carbon dot loops round and round.

shape.explain: The sun: energy enters the system once, as light.
Plants: they capture the sun's energy.
Animals: they get energy by eating plants.
The leak: most energy escapes as heat, never to return.
One unit of energy: unlike the carbon atom, it flows one way and escapes as heat.
A carbon atom's round trip: matter recycles.
Carbon held in plants.
Carbon held in animals.
Carbon as air CO2.
One carbon atom, looping through the living world.

steps.text: Energy flows one way; matter loops back
